questions.help:
ILLNESS AND MEDICATION
 
20 Some illnesses that can affect driving
20.1 Respiratory allergies
Allergic rhinitis can reduce the psycho-physical fitness to drive by up to 42%, causing alterations such as the loss of efficiency, lack of attention, a lower concentration level and decreased ability of visual coordination. It reduces the ability to judge stopping distance, thus increasing the risk of a collision.
The most common symptoms of this illness are very similar to those of a simple cold: Runny nose, watery eyes, blurred vision, bouts of sneezing (sometimes up to 20 in a row), fatigue, headache, and so on.
(Página 46 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help:
12 Distances
 
12.2 The braking distance
The braking distance is the distance the vehicle travels from the point at which the driver first applies the brakes, until the vehicle come to a complete stop.
This distance can vary depending on:
The speed of the vehicle at the point the brakes are applied.
The mass of the vehicle and its load.
The technical condition of the vehicle (brakes, tyres, shock absorbers, etc.)
The environmental conditions and the condition of the road surface (snow, rain, state of the surface, etc.)
The driver (psychophysical status –mental and physical state, experience, etc.)
An increase in speed causes the braking distance to increase, but this is at a greater rate than the speed increase.
Thus, when the velocity is doubled the braking distance is four times higher.
(Página 179 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help:
ACTIVE SAFETY FEATURES      
       
4 Wheels    
4.2 Tyres  
4.2.3 The tread pattern
The tread pattern is the set of grooves in the tread of a tire. In addition to gripping the road surface, it must guarantee good drainage away of the surface water from the tyre. The adhesion between the tyre and the road is reduced when the tyre is worn.
All tyres, (including retreads) must always comply with the legal requirements. This includes, not only the tyre tread and depth of pattern but also other abnormalities relating to the tyre-wall and tread, inflation pressure, bulges, exposed cords, cuts and other signs of irregular wear, and also the mixing of tyres etc. Basically the carcass (housing) must comply with all legal requirements.
Tyres must, throughout their use on public roads, have a depth in the main grooves of the tread which must be at least:
1.6 millimetres for vehicles in categories M1, N1, O1 and O2.
1.0 millimetres for vehicles in categories M2, M3, N2, N3, O3 and O4.
(Página 70 del manual 'Learning to drive')

ACTIVE SAFETY FEATURES      
       
4 Wheels    
4.2 Tyres  
4.2.3 The tread pattern
Regrooving (which consists of recutting part of the tread pattern into the tyre) are not allowed, except on tyres for vehicles over 3.5 tons of MAM and that clearly display the word “Regroovable” or the symbol U.
Tyres used on cars and trailers, which comply with legal requirements, must also have ‘tyre wear indicators’ (or TWI). The purpose of the tyre wear indicators is to indicate that the main grooves (within the central band) have reached the minimum depth of tread permitted.
Drivers must maintain their tyre and ensure that the tread reaches the required legal standard. It is advisable to replace them when the depth of the pattern is below 2 mm.
(Página 70 del manual 'Learning to drive')

7 Special circumstances regarding the circulation of traffic and the utilisation of lanes  
 
7.4 Additional circulation lane
All vehicles that travel in any of the lanes must:
Take special care to avoid colliding with the cones and other safety elements placed to create the change or road layout.
Travel at a maximum speed of 80 km/h and a minimum speed of 60 km/h.
Use during daylight hours and at night, at least low beam headlights.
Not enter into a lane where traffic is travelling in an opposite direction.
(Página 166 del manual 'Learning to drive')

7 ‘U’ turn    
7.3 Circumstances when it is prohibited to undertake a ‘U’ turn
It is specifically prohibited to carry out a ‘U’ turn:
At level crossings (although it is not prohibited in their immediate surroundings).
In tunnels, underpasses and sections of the road affected by the signal “unnel”.
On motorways and dual carriageways, except in the places designated for this purpose.
On one-way roads and one-way sections of roads.
In general, in all sections of the road where overtaking is prohibited, unless a ‘’turn is expressly authorized.
(Página 195 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help:
Journeys and defensive and efficient driving      
         
DEFENSIVE DRIVING      
4 Observation    
4.3 Use of mirrors and monitor the blind spot  
4.3.2 Blind Spot Monitoring (BSM)
The system warns the driver of the presence of another vehicle in the next lane in the blind spot by displaying a light in the rear-view mirror on that side. The most effective systems only give this warning when the driver uses the indicators to change lane.
There are other more advanced systems that can act on the steering and brakes; when the driver tries to switch to a lane occupied by another vehicle, they apply resistance to the steering wheel and slightly reduce the vehicle’s speed.
(Página 273 del manual 'Learning to drive')
